run: Pocket-TTS Farsi v2 scored on this project's development set, by the same protocol as every other engine
why: A Persian-specific cloning model appeared on 2026-09-14 (mehdi-hf/pocket-tts-farsi-v2, announced 2026-09-19 and packaged as nimaone/persian_tts): 109.5 M parameters trained on 973 h of Persian from 2,978 speakers - 7.6 times this project's own 128 h adaptation - reading romanised phonemes through Homo-GE2PE and running on a CPU. Its authors report speaker similarity 0.859 and median per-item WER 0.333 on 300 held-out Common Voice pairs. Those are their encoder, their reference and their test set, so they answer nothing about this project's question. This run answers it.

what_was_run.engine: pocket, added in ff8101e, by the model card's own recipe: normalise with the normalize_fa.py shipped beside the weights, phonemise with mehdi-hf/Homo-GE2PE-Persian-HF (num_beams 5), apply the card's symbol table, strip the ezafe mark before the model, split into sentences first, chunk budget 18 tokens, retry a generation that passes the card's duration cap
what_was_run.corpus: eval/corpus, 9 speakers (8 Common Voice, 1 studio), sentences s1-s3, seed 42, 27 renders
what_was_run.scoring: speechbrain ECAPA against held-out recordings of the same speaker, this Mac, 2026-09-20
what_was_run.comparison: the stored OmniVoice renders of the same 27 cells re-scored in this same session (label omnivoice-rescored), so similarity and CER are like-for-like

measured.paired: -0.2503 over the same 27 cells, 7.6 standard errors from zero, worse in 26 of 27
measured.scale: 0.132 floor, 0.689 human ceiling, 0.508 the highest different-speaker pair on this corpus
measured.reading: 0.333 sits below that 0.508: on this corpus these renders are not reliably distinguishable from a different speaker's

the_integration_was_checked_before_the_r.prompt_length: the prompt is a prefix this model continues from and its training utterances averaged 3.8 s, so the 11.4 s window could have been the handicap. Measured on 4 speakers x 3 sentences: 4 s gives 0.412, 6 s gives 0.388, the whole window gives 0.381 for the same four. Better, and nowhere near the gap
the_integration_was_checked_before_the_r.their_own_samples: [the decisive check] the three samples mehdi-hf ships with the weights, rendered by the authors from their own ~5 s prompts, score 0.321, 0.368 and 0.346 against those prompts on this project's ECAPA - below the 0.410-0.500 this integration gets. Whatever is being measured here, it is not a fault in the wiring
the_integration_was_checked_before_the_r.flags: the model was loaded from the card's own model.yaml and reports capitalize_first_letter, append_terminal_punctuation and pad_with_spaces_for_short_inputs all false - the three that otherwise delete or corrupt the first word
the_integration_was_checked_before_the_r.intelligibility: the recogniser reads the renders as the intended sentences (CER 2-14% per render), so nothing is generating noise

what_this_does_not_say: Nothing here compares with the authors' 0.859: a different encoder against a different reference on a different set. Their number is not reproduced or disputed, it is simply not on this scale
Nobody has listened to any of these renders. This is one encoder's opinion about identity, not a judgement of how they sound
CER is compared only inside this one scoring session, as this project's rule requires
Eight of the nine development speakers are Common Voice, which both models were very probably trained on. That caveat cuts both ways and is exactly why the sealed test exists
This is the development set. It decides what gets carried forward, not what is true
where_it_is_better: cost. 0.45 GiB of weights, loads in about 4 s, renders about 2 s of speech per 1.4 s of CPU - no GPU, no 6 GB of free memory, no separate 3 GB engine. Against the corpus's own 7.8% recogniser floor its 8.9% CER is roughly the intelligibility of real speech
consequence: OmniVoice stays the engine this project adapts. Pocket-TTS stays registered as an engine and a measured reference point, and is the only engine here that synthesises from Homo-GE2PE phonemes - the family of the Persian G2P research beside this project
